1. Task, evidence and schema handling
We predict categorical survey answers from each held-out respondent's GIVEN block for UNICEF Faith &
Immunisation, World Bank Skills Assessment and UNHCR ERPIS. Every PREDICT cell is blanked and scored;
EXCLUDE items are omitted. One self-contained predictor learns separately per instrument using complete visible
respondents, combining hierarchical smoothing, a shared neural network, approximate skip logic and similar-row
donor evidence. No fitted state is bundled.
E025 is a preserved alternative to provisional E041, not a user-selected final TEST model. Its historical user-reported
DEV readings were Grand 0.63, UNICEF 0.52, World Bank 0.49 and UNHCR 0.89. E041's later released API record
ID933094 reports 0.6433333333/0.52/0.49/0.92 (Grand displayed as 0.64). These retained readings remain subject to
phase-1 Laplace noise and 0.01 rounding. Extra serialized decimals do not establish precise effects. They compare
adaptively developed complete pipelines, not independent component trials. No real TEST score exists; E064 is
parked awaiting DEV delivery, with no actual hosted result. [6,7]
Phase 1 shows TRAIN and scores DEV; phase 2 shows TRAIN+DEV and scores TEST. The pinned kit describes
shuffled respondent roles, stratified by country for UNICEF and balanced by survey round/country for UNHCR, with
ordinary permutation for World Bank. This is not a chronological or new-country holdout. Same-population split
relevance does not guarantee refit gain or repair adaptive DEV selection. [1,6]
The official metric averages log probabilities over all scored cells within an instrument, then scales by schema-only
uniform surprisal U. Grand is the equally weighted mean of the three instrument skills. K includes the sentinel for
gated items. Confident errors are costly.
skill = 1 + mean_cells(log p'_[true answer]) / U
U = mean_scored_items(log K_i)
Vectors follow schema item/option order, adding NA_GATED as the last option for gated items. NaN means predict;
refusal and other non-response categories remain ordinary answers. Decoding passes parents' final beliefs, including
donor evidence, to descendants. A visible parent gives a one-hot belief. For gated item i, r_i is parent mass on
observed-if values.
hard_i = [r_i * asked_conditional_i, 1 - r_i]
base_i = a_i(x) * hard_i + (1 - a_i(x)) * full_i
Asked-conditional heads train on asked rows; unrestricted full heads include the sentinel. UNHCR gate agreement is
approximate (median 0.83, range 0.29-0.98), so hard coupling can be wrong even with a known parent. Scalar
agreement (k_i+20*m)/(n_i+20) shrinks toward median observed agreement m, not one. For each child, an internal
20% split can select one GIVEN column of cardinality at most 12; its value-specific rates shrink toward the scalar.
Without improvement the scalar remains. [1,6]

2. Runtime prediction, donor matching and replay
Hierarchical backoff.
A smoothed global marginal anchors a ladder, with each level adding a GIVEN column.
Column order, depth up to three and kappa in {1,3,10,30,100} are selected greedily by held-out log score on 20% of
complete visible rows. Candidate columns have at most 12 levels. Asked-only distributions use the same ladder;
sparse cells borrow strength and unseen cells back off.
p_L(v | cell) = (n_L(v) + kappa_L*p_(L-1)(v)) / (N_L+kappa_L)
Shared trunk.
One-hot GIVEN inputs feed a Linear-ReLU network with softmax full heads for PREDICT items and
separate asked-only heads for gated items. Masked cross-entropy pools observed full and conditional targets.
Full-batch Adam uses learning rate 0.003, weight decay 0.0001, at most 500 epochs and patience 30 on an inner split.
An outer split chooses two 64-unit layers/no dropout or two 128-unit layers/dropout 0.1. The selected epoch count is
refitted on all complete visible rows. One instrument-level network/ladder mixing weight from {0,0.1,...,1} is
selected on the outer split and shared by full and conditional heads. Fixed split and network seeds are zero.
Visible-row evidence.
Every complete visible respondent is a potential donor, without a cross-round restriction.
Matching uses GIVEN values, never respondent identifiers. Initial weights are -log(u_j), where u_j is random
agreement estimated from available GIVEN frequencies, including held-out GIVEN covariates. That covariate use
does not include held-out PREDICT responses.
A preliminary match identifies provisional pairs with top posterior mass at least 0.5. With at least 30 such pairs, one
Fellegi-Sunter-style update estimates per-column agreement m_j; otherwise the rarity weights remain. Weighted
GIVEN agreement is normalized with softmax over the top ten donors, whose answer vectors supply item evidence.
weight_j = max(0, log(m_j/u_j) - log((1-m_j)/(1-u_j)))
This soft neighborhood can exploit ordinary similarity or near-duplicate structure; it does not establish household
relationships or identities. An organizer ruling retained in the project allows matching within the supplied dataset
without external identity linkage. We do not assert newly authenticated organizer correspondence or link to external
records. [6]
Concentration-specific calibration.
Self-excluded replay uses up to 6,000 complete visible queries. For each item,
lambda is chosen from {0,0.1,...,0.9,0.95,0.98}, separately when maximum donor mass is below or at least 0.5. Each
bucket requires 30 valid observations; insufficient support leaves lambda zero. The query is excluded as its own
donor. The final update follows gate mixing and precedes descendants' decoding.
final_i = (1-lambda_i) * base_i + lambda_i * evidence_i
No positive learned lambda means base-only prediction. No usable GIVEN signature supplies no evidence. GPU
training exceptions can use CPU fallback; arbitrary whole-run failures and timeouts do not create a new TEST
attempt.
E025 has no E041 learned section metric, 32-candidate reranking, metric-fit/selection/replay partition
or section activation gate.
Its two-architecture choice, top-ten donors, replay cap and lambda grid are unchanged.

3. Calibration limits, development evidence and phase-2 refit
Ladder selection, conditional agreement, architecture/epoch choice and network mixing use internal visible-row
splits. Donor replay excludes self-matches, but base predictions are refitted on all visible rows, including replay
labels. Self-exclusion therefore does not cross-fit calibration, and replay performance is not an unbiased
generalization estimate. No E041 partitioning is implicitly credited to E025, and no repair of this optimism is
claimed.
Algorithm choices and grids were developed through synthetic work, public instrument descriptions and repeated
DEV feedback. Parameters are estimated at runtime, but the retained method was selected adaptively during
development. Legal TRAIN+DEV final fitting does not make those DEV observations independent again. Fixed
seeds do not prevent row-order, CPU/GPU or reduction-related numerical variation. [6]
Complete phase-2 visible counts grow to 16,373 UNICEF, 5,715 World Bank and 8,900 UNHCR respondents. Every
fitted component is rebuilt from that frame: adding DEV can change marginals, asked-only heads, ladder
order/shrinkage, network architecture/epochs/mixing, gate coefficients, agreement weights and replay lambdas. The
larger visible bank may help or hurt; no linear runtime or gain forecast follows. Larger replay caps, ensembles,
identifier signatures, tree blends and relation-specific evidence variants are not part of this predictor.
Development counterevidence.
Six later hosted comparisons were flat at displayed resolution: evidence as network
input (E027), parent-value gate decoding (E028), larger replay (E031b), relation-specific weights (E036), identifier
signatures (E038) and a tree blend (E040). Simulation gains under injected assumptions did not establish transfer.
E037 sentinel recalibration gained about 0.024 in-sample on a heavy-overlap simulation but lost about 0.004 under
cross-fitting and was rejected. These observations neither prove zero possible improvement nor justify another
same-policy attempt. [6]
E032-E034 aggregate UNHCR probes describe E025 only: approximate skill 0.79 from the base plus 0.10 from
evidence, with remaining loss about 0.079 gated/0.031 ungated. Keeping sentinel mass while flattening asked
answers left gated skill near 0.56. These are model-performance summaries, not private response statistics or an
E041 decomposition. Rounded/noised same-phase Grand differences imply coarse practical UNHCR resolution,
about 0.015-0.03, not three-decimal precision. E032 initially changed all instruments and used a second account,
later retired and flagged as a likely Terms violation. No adjudication, waiver or independent replication is asserted.
Separate Adult/SIPP studies address limited proxy channels. E053 and E055 oracle STOPs do not bound
approximate UNHCR calibration; later E056-E059 supplied no deployed component. E059 STOP_SELECTION and
A_half nonpromotion remain. Later E060/E062/E063 released ties leave effects unresolved; E061's adverse result
applies to that complete pipeline. E064 local qualification supplies no actual hosted score. No result from these
alternatives changes this draft's E025 identity or final-choice status. [6,7]
Engineering scope.
Public synthetic phase-2 TEST-role cells were previously exposed development material, not
newly independent real TEST evidence. The completed E025 provenance task below closes a concrete
source/archive/data/scorer connection; it does not validate hidden humanitarian population structure, establish E025
superiority or remove selection/calibration uncertainty. No raw response values appear in this document.

1996; CC BY 4.0), Census 2023 SIPP public-use observations and Prior Labs TabPFN V2 experiments. A040 used
